result:
I found 11 rules whose behaviour didn't match their docstrings and fixed all of them in `pricebook.py`.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 01 | The discount started at 11 units instead of 10 | `qty >= 11` → `qty >= 10` |
| 66 | The discount started at 11 units instead of 10 | `qty > 10` → `qty >= 10` |
| 04 | The discount was rounded instead of floored | `round(...)` → `// 100` |
| 117 | The discount was rounded instead of floored | `round(...)` → `// 100` |
| 121 | The discount was rounded instead of floored | `round(...)` → `// 100` |
| 44 | The cap was applied to the price instead of the discount | Calculate 10% of the full price, then cap the discount at 30,000 won |
| 79 | The cap was applied to the price instead of the discount | Calculate 10% of the full price, then cap the discount at 100,000 won |
| 129 | The cap was applied to the price instead of the discount | Calculate 10% of the full price, then cap the discount at 30,000 won |
| 93 | It took 4% off instead of 3% | 4 → 3 |
| 96 | A "whole" rule only discounted the units above the threshold | Apply the discount to the full price (`base * 5 // 100`) |
| 123 | The cap only kicked in once the discount went over 200,000 won | Always cap the discount at 100,000 won |

**How I checked:** I wrote a script that reads each docstring, works out the correct price from it, and compares that with what all 150 functions return for quantities 0–259, 500, 1,000 and 5,000 and a range of unit prices. Before the fixes it found these 11 mismatches; after the fixes it found none. All 150 functions also still raise an error on negative inputs.

STATUS: DONE
